messages:
danielle: Quick note: ran into flaky auth during a demo where we rotate API keys in-place. wanted to surface proposed SDK behavior.
omar: what flaky behavior did you see?
danielle: We have a long-lived process calling Redwood. We rotated creds via a local helper that writes ~/.redwood/creds.json and sets REDWOOD_API_KEY. New calls used the new key but retries for in-flight requests kept using the old one and looped 401s.
leigh: sounds like the token was captured at request start and reused for retries. That makes rotations painful.
danielle: Exactly. In our setup the rotate tool does atomic rename (tmp -> creds.json) and then exports the env var. Some SDKs missed the change when watching inode alone.
omar: Proposed policy: (1) env var checked on each request but token cached for a short TTL (default 2s) to avoid KMS thrashing; (2) on retry after auth failure (401/403) force a refresh and re-send; (3) REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID / REDWOOD_ORG_ID should be init-only — if they change at runtime, log+throw and require restart.
leigh: I like that. Also add opt-out: REDWOOD_CRED_HOTRELOAD=false for deterministic infra tests and a client-level option credHotReload for per-client control.
danielle: Implementation details for file-backed creds: don't rely on mtime alone. Use mtime + cheap checksum (sha1 prefix) or small file hash. On platforms with overlayfs/atomic renames we saw mtime sometimes unchanged for a brief window.
omar: For performance: quick path checks env mtime; if mtime differs spawn background hash compute then swap if hash changed. For tiny creds file cost is negligible and keeps request path fast.
leigh: API suggestion: expose client.refreshCredentials(force=false) so orchestration tools can call post-rotation. Also ensure SDKs re-fetch token on auth-retry only, not on every retry. Parity note: python client already does this, js/go need to match.
danielle: Add a short info-level log when token source switches (env -> file -> kms) and when a retry triggers a credential refresh. This makes local debugging much faster.
sre-bot: CI: added integration test rotate-inflight.sh to flaky-tests job (will rotate creds mid-request and assert client recovers) :construction_worker:
leigh: docs: update SDK README to clearly state env precedence (REDWOOD_API_KEY overrides file), the init-only invariants for project/org env vars, and recommended rotation patterns (export env + call refresh API). Provide sample script.
danielle: sample rotate script for example app: ```sh
# examples/rotate-local.sh
# write new creds then export and signal app to refresh
echo '{"api_key":"NEW_LOCAL_TOKEN"}' > ~/.redwood/creds.json
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=NEW_LOCAL_TOKEN
# if using client refresh API:
node -e "require('./example-client').client.refreshCredentials(true)"
# or curl a control endpoint the app exposes to call refresh
curl -sS http://localhost:3000/-/refresh || true
```
omar: also include a note about atomic rename: if your rotate tool writes tmp file then mv into place, the SDK's checksum+mtime check will reliably detect change.
leigh: logging detail: emit something like: "info: cred source switched env->file; previous=env" and "info: auth-retry triggered credential refresh". Keep logs low-volume.
danielle: created GH issue #1991 to track cross-SDK parity and sample app updates. tagging @eng-sdk.
eng-sdk: PR incoming for js/go to add credHotReload, Client.refreshCredentials, retry-on-401 refresh, and file checksum detection. CI will add the rotate-inflight integration.
sre-bot: PR preview: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/1200 - feat: cred hot-reload + retry refresh (CI: queued) :ramen:
danielle: thanks all. once PR lands I'll validate on my laptop and in our containerized demo. If anyone wants to test the sample script ping me and I'll share a small test harness.
